name: TX-16
label: Safe D

key_factors: D+11 district with incumbent Veronica Escobar seeking another term
Fundraising gap: Escobar has raised $1.03M vs. under $3K for Adam Bauman
Prediction markets price a Democratic hold near 97%
No public polling; the margin rests on fundamentals
model.rationale: An eleven-point Democratic district, a running incumbent, and a fundraising advantage of roughly 350-to-1 leave Bauman without a visible path, and markets price the seat as safely Democratic. The only real uncertainty is the size of the margin, since no public polls are available.
model.watch: A late wave of outside spending on Bauman's behalf or a sharp national shift toward Republicans could narrow the margin, though the seat itself is very unlikely to come into play.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Veronica Escobar enters the general election as a heavy favorite in an El Paso-based district that leans Democratic by eleven points. She has raised more than one million dollars for the race, while Republican Adam Bauman has reported under three thousand in contributions and minimal cash on hand. Prediction markets put the Democratic chance of holding the seat near ninety-seven percent, and no major rating organizations flag the contest as competitive.

With no public polling available, the exact margin carries some uncertainty, but every fundamental points the same direction: the district's partisan lean, Escobar's incumbency, and an overwhelming financial edge. The expected outcome is a Democratic win of roughly twenty-three points. Barring an unexpected shift in the national environment, this district is firmly in the Democratic column.
